subject: Post-call: FinBank evals / recommended models & next steps

Subject: Post-call: FinBank evals / recommended models & next steps

Hi Tom — thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Highlights from the call:
- Primary use case: customer support response generation for retail banking (intent classification + short-form response).
- Success metrics: intent classification accuracy >= 92%, response helpfulness MOS >= 4.0 for core intents, latency p95 under 300ms for single-turn responses.
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction required; FinBank prefers VPC/private deployment for production but is open to hosted evals for initial benchmarking.

Recommended immediate steps:
1) Run a FinBank-specific eval suite on Redwood with your sample dataset (small pilot: ~2k prompts). Please see the attached eval template (finbank_eval_template.csv) and README for formatting notes.
2) We'll seed the eval with two model candidates for your workload: RW-Accel-7B (low-latency, cost-effective for rapid prototyping) and RW-Prod-13B-Quant (higher quality, quantized for cost/throughput balance). If you'd like to consider third-party models, we can add Llama2-13B-Chat (quant) for comparison.
3) Scoring: intent accuracy (strict match), semantic similarity for responses (embedding-based cosine + human MOS sample), and a regression check against your current baseline.
4) Security: For the hosted eval we will enable KV prefix stripping and ensure audit logging. If you want the artifacts kept within your VPC, we can schedule a Private eval run (requires NDA/PO).

Next actions for this week:
- Tom: share a 1-2k sample of de-identified prompts + expected labels (upload to the Drive link we discussed) — target: EOD Wednesday (7/21).
- Marissa/Neha: set up the eval project in Redwood, include the scoring rubric and baseline reference, and provide the run link.
- If procurement needs a statement of work or security docs let me know and I’ll loop in legal.

I attached the CSV template and a quickstart that explains how to format prompts and expected outputs. If anything in the template looks off for your label schema, we’ll adjust it.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Tom — yes, 30-day log retention for the hosted eval is configurable. We’ll set that as the default for this pilot and document it in the run summary.

Below are more details on the eval setup, recommended model configs, prompt sets, dataset format, and scoring criteria so your team can review ahead of upload.

1) Recommended models / configs (initial pilot):
- RW-Accel-7B: streaming-enabled, batch-size=4, kv-cache enabled, target p95 < 300ms for single-turn prompts. Low cost per-token. Good first gate to validate latency and intent classification via few-shot prompts.
- RW-Prod-13B-Quant: 8-bit quantized for production-quality responses, batch-size=8, recommended for quality/regression testing against baseline. Expect higher MOS but slightly higher latency.
- Optional: Llama2-13B-Chat (quant) as a third-party comparator (if you want an open-model baseline).

2) Prompt set & dataset format (see attached finbank_eval_template.csv):
- Required columns: id, prompt, expected_label, expected_response, category, sensitivity_flag
- Sensitivity: please set sensitivity_flag = redacted for any PII rows. We recommend removing account numbers and replacing with placeholders.
- Suggested volume: 2k prompts for the pilot (balanced across categories). If you can provide a stratified sample (by category and intent frequency) that will make the metrics more actionable.

3) Scoring criteria (automated + human):
- Intent accuracy: strict match on expected_label (primary gate).
- Response semantic match: embedding cosine similarity between model response and expected_response (thresholds: >=0.85 strong, 0.7-0.85 partial).
- MOS (human): human-evaluated mean opinion score on a 1-5 scale for a random 200-sample per model.
- Regression checks: automatic diff vs. baseline model on intent accuracy and embedding similarity. Flag any >3% drop in accuracy or >0.1 drop in mean embedding similarity.
- Latency: p50/p95 token latency per model.

4) Redwood eval run setup (how we’ll run it for you):
- We’ll create an Eval Project in your account and upload the template to a private evaluation bucket. For hosted pilot runs we’ll use a dedicated sandbox project with 30-day logs.
- You’ll get an Eval run link (see related_links) that contains run-level metrics, per-sample outputs, and a downloadable results CSV.
- We can enable per-sample redaction and a flag indicating which responses hit a PII placeholder so you can exclude them from MOS grading.

5) Deliverables & timeline:
- Day 0 (when we receive data): ingest and quick sanity check (~1 business day).
- Day 1-2: run both models on 2k prompts, deliver raw outputs + metrics.
- Day 3: collect MOS sample and consolidate final report with recommendations (model pick, quantization profile, cost estimates).

If this all looks good I’ll set up the Eval Project and send the run link once the sample is uploaded. If you prefer we can walk your engineers through the upload and run process — Neha can lead that session.

Marissa
